# featbit_project (Resource)

Manages a FeatBit Project through the documented public API.

Terraform owns the Project `name` and `key`. The key defines replacement
identity; changing it creates a replacement instead of adopting an existing
exact-key Project. FeatBit's server-created Environments are exposed through
`environments` as canonical, non-owning observations. Manage additional
Environments with `featbit_environment`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "featbit_project" "example" {
  name = "Checkout service"
  key  = "checkout-service"
}
```

## Lifecycle

- `name` updates in place.
- `key` requires replacement.
- An out-of-band deletion is removed from Terraform state only after the
  complete Project collection proves exact absence.
- Destroy sends one delete request and preserves state whenever exact absence
  cannot be proven. Destroy child resources first.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Immutable Project key.
- `name` (String) Project display name.

### Read-Only

- `environments` (Attributes List) Canonical, non-owning observations of the Project environments. Manage additional environments with featbit_environment. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--environments))
- `id` (String) Project UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--environments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `environments`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) Environment description.
- `id` (String) Environment UUID.
- `key` (String) Environment key.
- `name` (String) Environment display name.

## Import

Import a Project with its exact UUID:

```shell
terraform import featbit_project.example '<project_uuid>'
```

The identifier must be one UUID in 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form.
